title: How the day closed
text: The big story today was NVIDIA. The company said Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and left its board of directors. Its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, is now interim CEO while the board looks for a permanent leader. NVIDIA fell more than 13% early in the day, touching $148.80, a new one year low. It then recovered part of the drop and closed at $166.19, down 4.3%. Rivals AMD (up 5.9%) and Broadcom (up 5.5%) rose. The whole market barely moved: the S&P 500 fund SPY and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ each slipped about 0.3%. One company's bad day does not always mean a bad day for everyone.

title: NVIDIA bounced off a new one year low
text: NVIDIA closed about 12% above its low of the day. That kind of swing in a single day shows how nervous investors are. Our risk score for NVIDIA rose from 5.7 to 6.0, still in the medium zone. The average analyst price target is still about $328, but targets can change quickly after big news like this.

title: AMD and Broadcom climbed while NVIDIA fell
text: AMD closed at $585.30 and is now near the top of its one year range, about 11% below its high. Broadcom closed at $364.36. Both make chips that compete with NVIDIA's. Some investors seem to think customers could shift some orders to them. That is a guess about the future, not a fact yet.

title: Bond yields are back near 5%
text: The 10 year Treasury yield, the interest rate the US government pays to borrow for 10 years, moved back near 5% after a hot inflation report. Traders are betting the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its December 9 meeting. Another price report, the producer price index, comes out Friday. When safe bonds pay more, some investors need a stronger reason to own riskier stocks.

title: Lesson 49: What is succession planning?
text: Succession planning means deciding ahead of time who could take over if a company's leader leaves. Leaders can leave for many reasons: they retire, get sick, or step down after a problem. If a company has a clear plan, the change is calmer. If it does not, investors worry about who will make the big decisions. When NVIDIA's CEO resigned, the board named its chief financial officer, the person in charge of the money, as interim CEO. Interim means temporary: she leads while the board searches for a permanent CEO. Think of a sports team whose coach leaves in the middle of the season. An assistant coach steps in so the team keeps playing. When you study a company, it is fair to ask: does it depend too much on one person?
